author: Liam O'Connor
title: St Finbarr's Edge Out Nemo Rangers in Division 1 Football League Clash
text:
Trabeg, County Cork – St. Finbarr’s continued their recent dominance over Nemo Rangers with a hard-fought 0-10 to 0-9 victory in Wednesday evening’s McCarthy Insurance Group Division 1 Football League clash. The win, a repeat of last year’s Premier SFC final which the Barrs also won by a single point, moves Brian Roche’s side to five points after three rounds of the league. For Nemo Rangers, it’s a second consecutive loss, leaving them on two points and facing early questions in the campaign.
The match, played under challenging conditions with a tricky wind and intermittent showers, was a tense affair marked by turnovers and missed opportunities for both sides. While a draw felt like a fair outcome for much of the contest, a late point from Bill O’Connell proved decisive, extending St. Finbarr’s winning streak against their southside rivals. This latest encounter underscores the growing rivalry between the two Cork footballing giants, a dynamic that continues to captivate local fans.
Early Exchanges and Nemo’s First-Half Push
St. Finbarr’s started brightly, with early points from Cillian Myers-Murray and John Wigginton-Barrett establishing a foothold in the game. But, the opening stages were characterized by a lack of fluency, with both teams struggling to maintain possession. Jack O’Brien opened the scoring for Nemo Rangers after 11 minutes, sparking a period of competitive exchanges. A brace of points from Ross Corkery then propelled Nemo Rangers into the lead, a position they held thanks to the effectiveness of Eoin Nation and Eoin Kelly around the middle of the field.
Nemo Rangers capitalized on their momentum with a goal from Ronan Dalton before halftime, giving them a 0-6 to 0-4 advantage at the break. This scoreline represented a significant shift in the game’s narrative, putting pressure on St. Finbarr’s to respond in the second half. The first half also saw some early injury concerns for both sides, foreshadowing a physical contest.
Barrs Rally and a Tightly Contested Second Half
The second half saw a swift response from St. Finbarr’s, with Conor Dennehy and Myers-Murray quickly leveling the score. The momentum continued to swing as Myers-Murray, proving to be a constant threat, added another point to put the Barrs ahead. However, Nemo Rangers refused to yield, with Corkery again finding the target to restore parity.
The second 30 minutes were disjointed, punctuated by stoppages and a high degree of physicality. Substitute Dara O’Sullivan briefly put Nemo Rangers ahead with a late surge, but Myers-Murray responded with a crucial free to tie the game at 0-9 apiece as the clock ticked down. The tension was palpable as both teams sought a winning score.
O’Connell Secures Late Victory for the Barrs
With the game poised for a draw, Bill O’Connell stepped forward to slot over the winning point, securing a 0-10 to 0-9 victory for St. Finbarr’s. The late score highlighted the Barrs’ resilience and their ability to perform under pressure. The winning point, coming in the dying moments, was a testament to O’Connell’s composure and accuracy.
Cillian Myers-Murray finished as the game’s top scorer with 0-6, including one penalty and a free, demonstrating his importance to the St. Finbarr’s attack. Ross Corkery led the scoring for Nemo Rangers with 0-3. A full breakdown of the scores can be found below:

The teams lined up as follows:
NEMO RANGERS: F Dietze; C Moore, M Hill, N O’Shea; E Nation, S Cronin, T O’Brien; E Kelly, J O’Brien; O Whyte, R Dalton, L Horgan; R Corkery, C Horgan, S Burke. Subs: D O’Sullivan for S Burke (h-t), A O’Donovan for O Whyte (41), B O’Neill for J O’Brien (43, inj).
ST FINBARR’S: C Haynes; D Quinn, J Burns, T Howe; B Hennessy, A O’Connor, C Dennehy; I O’Callaghan, C Crowley; B O’Connell, E Dennehy, A Lyne; C O’Sullivan, J Wigginton-Barrett, C Myers-Murray. Subs: C Doolan for C Crowley (41), S Kirby for I O’Callaghan (49, inj), J Kennefick for C Dennehy (57, inj).
James Regan of Lough Rovers served as the referee for the match. The Echo reports that injuries to Ian O’Callaghan and Conor Dennehy added to the challenges faced by St. Finbarr’s.
St. Finbarr’s will appear to continue their winning form in their next league fixture, while Nemo Rangers will aim to get back on track and address the issues that have plagued their start to the season. The competitive nature of the Cork Division 1 Football League promises further exciting clashes as the season progresses.
